title: Implement notes schema and add_note
summary: Created app.py with an idempotent SQLite schema initializer and add_note(title, body). The notes table uses SQLite stdlib with columns id, title, body, and created_at; add_note returns the new note ID. No ORM, no list_notes, and no test suite were added. Verified against a temporary notes.db: schema created idempotently, two notes inserted with IDs 1 and 2, values round-tripped, and quoting worked.

title: Add list_notes and pytest test suite
summary: Added list_notes() to app.py and a pytest suite in test_app.py. list_notes returns a list of dicts (id, title, body, created_at) ordered newest first via ORDER BY created_at DESC, id DESC (id tiebreak because CURRENT_TIMESTAMP is second-precision). Added an optional db_path parameter to init_db/add_note/list_notes, defaulting to DB_PATH, so tests inject a tmp_path database and never touch the real notes.db. Five pytest tests cover init_db idempotency, add_note IDs/round-trip, quote preservation, newest-first ordering, and lazy DB creation. Ran `python -m pytest test_app.py -q`: 5 passed. No notes.db was created in the repo.

title: Split notes app into app package and add search_notes
summary: Reversed the single-file decision: deleted app.py and split it into an app package. app/db.py now holds DB_PATH, SCHEMA, _connect, init_db, add_note, list_notes, and the new search_notes(query); app/main.py is the CLI entry point (`python -m app.main`); app/__init__.py re-exports the db API so existing `import app` call sites keep working. DB_PATH still resolves to notes.db at the project root. search_notes does a case-insensitive substring match over title OR body, escapes % and _ so they are literal, and orders newest first like list_notes. Added two pytest tests (title/body/case/no-match and literal wildcards). Full suite: 7 passed. Port convention updated in Mesh from 4010 to 3100; no code in the repo referenced a port, so no code change was needed for it.
